current_episode.title: How batteries can reduce fuel poverty and limit burgeoning grid costs

guest.titre: Opportunities Manager for Energy System Challenges
guest.bio_context: Davide Turi works at EON where his role is to identify opportunities to solve energy system challenges while lowering customer bills. He is actively involved in designing and piloting domestic battery programs targeting fuel-poor customers and working with distribution system operators to optimize grid flexibility.

context.real_quote: The fastest entry point is really getting a battery installed and let the battery do the hard work and eventually no need for changing your behavior.
key_stats: Average annual savings: £250 to £150 per year from time-of-use tariff alignment
Pilot guaranteed savings: £480 per year in constraint zones
Grid constraint analysis: at least 3.7 gigawatts in local distribution areas requiring infrastructure investment
Peak demand period: 4 to 7 in the afternoon when gas power plants are typically activated

pending_qa.q: How difficult is it to install a domestic battery in a home?
pending_qa.r: Installation takes half a day with no major changes required to home systems. An engineer simply screws a few holes in the wall, runs a cable, and customers can start saving from the day after installation. The process is designed to be simple with no app or technical setup required.

pending_qa.q: How can domestic batteries be made accessible to fuel-poor households and people in condensed housing?
pending_qa.r: EON is actively running pilots targeting fuel-poor customers to ensure they understand the opportunity to save money and avoid choosing between eating and heating their home. The company hopes the government will consider including batteries as part of broader interventions for helping customers. Batteries can be installed as standalone solutions without requiring air source heat pumps or major home modifications, making them accessible to residents in tower blocks and condensed housing.

pending_qa.q: What regulatory or policy support is needed to scale domestic battery adoption across the energy system?
pending_qa.r: Longer-term flexibility contracts with distribution system operators would allow confident investment in residential batteries at scale. Additionally, batteries should be included as a key measure in government warm-up plans to lower customer bills and fuel poverty. This would help distribute more batteries across the country and deliver direct benefits to customers while improving energy security.

pending_qa.q: What role will domestic batteries play in the future energy system over the next 10 years?
pending_qa.r: Batteries will play a key role alongside renewable energy sources, which are inherently unpredictable. The future energy system will feature large-scale batteries paired with hundreds of thousands of distributed batteries in homes, transforming them from passive consumers into active participants in the energy system. Simplicity in user experience will be essential to bring this flexibility technology into the mass market.
